The flaw exists in PyTorch's JIT (Just-In-Time) runtime, specifically within the tupleConstruct function in vararg\_functions.cpp. The vulnerability was identified through fuzzing efforts targeting the torch JIT lite interpreter, which revealed a read-heap-buffer-overflow condition. [...] A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in PyTorch before version v2.2.0 within the /runtime/vararg\_functions.cpp component. This vulnerability allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted input that triggers an out-of-bounds read operation in the heap memory. [...] The root cause stems from insufficient bounds checking when constructing tuples from the stack. When the tupleConstruct function is called with a num\_inputs parameter that exceeds the actual stack size, the function attempts to read beyond the allocated heap buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds memory access.
